mainTopic: Items that join with meat for טומאת אוכלין, and when drinking counts as eating
overview: The גמרא works through our משנה's list of things that join with meat to reach the size needed for טומאת אוכלין. ריש לקיש says only true protectors like bone count, so hair does not. רבי יוחנן says hair is also a שומר because it goes through the hide to the meat. When רב אחא asks how תפילין parchment could then be valid, the גמרא answers that a hole the ink covers is not a hole. רבי יוחנן's proof from a hair across from meat is answered by saying the hair is a handle (יד), as a hair among many hairs. The גמרא then defines רוטב as congealed fat and קיפה as spices, since those are not food on their own. A side discussion shows that drinking melted חלב, dissolved חמץ, or a liquefied bird נבלה still counts, because the word נפש includes one who drinks. The גמרא proves that all three mentions of נפש are needed. Last, it explains why a separate word is needed to forbid the liquids of שרצים: without it, the דיו rule would require a כזית.

steps.title: The argument is about our משנה's list of items that join with meat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the coming argument is about the משנה that lists hide, gravy, spices and similar items as joining with meat for טומאת אוכלין.
steps.simpleTranslation: This argument is about our משנה: 'The hide, the gravy, the spices, and so on' join together with the meat to make food impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move by telling us which משנה the argument is about. It quotes the משנה's list of things that join with meat for טומאת אוכלין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Food only becomes able to spread impurity once it reaches a minimum size. The משנה teaches that certain attached items, like hide, gravy and spices, count together with the meat toward that size. The next steps ask exactly which attached items count.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
They join together, adding up toward the required amount
The impurity of food
Gravy (here, congealed gravy stuck to the meat)
Spices or residue stuck to the meat

phrases.english: On our mishna: 'The hide and the gravy
and the spices, etc.'
join together to impart the impurity of food.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the discussion by naming the משנה the argument is about.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Hide, gravy, spices and similar attached items join with meat to reach the amount needed for טומאת אוכלין.

steps.title: ריש לקיש says bone counts as protection but hair does not
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש limits the משנה to items like bone that are a שומר, and says hair is not a שומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: The משנה only taught this about bone, because it is a protection. But a hair is not a protection.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש explains why the items in the משנה count: they protect the meat. Because of that, he says hair does not count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason something joins with the meat is that it acts as a שומר, a covering that protects the meat. Bone and the other listed items qualify. Hair, in ריש לקיש's view, does not protect the meat, so it does not join.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this about, which limits the scope of a teaching
Bone
A protector, an outer covering that guards the food
A hair

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
They taught this only about a bone,
because it is a protector,
but a hair is not a protector.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא עֶצֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains and limits the משנה from step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only true protectors like bone join with the meat. Hair is not a שומר and does not join.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן says hair also counts as protection
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן disagrees and holds that even hair is a שומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Even a hair is also a protection.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן disagrees with ריש לקיש. He says hair is also a שומר, so it joins with the meat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree on the rule that a שומר joins with the meat. They argue only about whether hair is a שומר. For רבי יוחנן it is, so hair adds toward the required amount.

keyTerms.meaning: Even ... also

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
Even a hair is also a protector.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ נִימָא נָמֵי הָוְיָא שׁוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to ריש לקיש in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Hair is a שומר and joins with the meat for טומאת אוכלין.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the whole back-and-forth that follows, which tests whether hair can really protect the meat.

steps.title: ריש לקיש asks how there can be a protection on top of a protection
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש challenges רבי יוחנן: the hide already protects the meat, and hair sits on top of the hide.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said to רבי יוחנן: Is there such a thing as a protection on top of a protection?
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש attacks רבי יוחנן's view. The hide is the meat's protection, and the hair only protects the hide, so how can hair count?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שומר counts because it guards the food directly. Hair grows on the hide, not on the meat, so at most it protects the hide. ריש לקיש assumes a second layer of covering does not count as the meat's שומר.

keyTerms.meaning: But is there? This is a challenging question
A protector on top of another protector

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Reish Lakish said to Rabbi Yochanan:
But is there such a thing as a protector
phrases.notes: The hide is the first protector of the meat, and the hair is on top of the hide.

phrases.english: on top of a protector?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אִיכָּא שׁוֹמֵר עַל גַּבֵּי שׁוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוחנן's ruling from step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's claim that hair is a שומר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Hair covers the hide, not the meat. A covering on top of another covering does not protect the meat itself.

steps.title: The hair pokes through the hide and reaches the meat
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that the hair goes through the hide and touches the meat directly.
steps.simpleTranslation: It penetrates through.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers ריש לקיש's question. The hair is not only on top of the hide; it goes through the hide down to the meat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the hair reaches the meat itself, it is not a second layer. It directly protects the meat, so it counts as the meat's own שומר and the 'protection on top of protection' problem goes away.

keyTerms.meaning: It really penetrates through

phrases.english: It penetrates through.
phrases.notes: This is רבי יוחנן's answer: the hair pushes through the hide and reaches the meat itself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers ריש לקיש's challenge in step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the physical facts: hair goes through the hide.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Hair sits only on top of the hide, so it can only protect the hide.
steps.terutzMaskana: Hair passes through the hide and touches the meat, so it directly protects the meat.
steps.confusionAlert: There is no speaker named here, but this is רבי יוחנן answering ריש לקיש, not the גמרא's own conclusion.

steps.title: רב אחא asks how תפילין could be written on hide full of holes
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא objects: if hair makes holes through the hide, תפילין parchment would have holes, and the letters need to be perfect.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא objected: If so, how do we write תפילין? We need perfect writing, and there would be none!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא challenges רבי יוחנן's answer. If every hair makes a hole through the hide, then the letters written on it would have holes in them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תפילין are written on parchment made from animal hide. The halacha requires כתיבה תמה, complete letters with no breaks. If hide is full of holes from hairs, it seems impossible ever to write valid תפילין.

keyTerms.meaning: He objects to it, a challenge to the previous statement
If that is so, which points out a problem that follows
תפילין, written on parchment made from hide
Perfect, complete writing with no breaks in the letters

phrases.english: Rav Acha objects to it:
If that is so,
how do we write tefillin?
But we require perfect writing,
and there is none!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אַחָא: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that hair penetrates through the hide
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If hide has holes wherever hairs pass through, letters written on parchment would be broken, so כתיבה תמה would be impossible.
steps.whyThisMatters: It ties a question about food impurity to a practical halacha of writing תפילין, testing whether the physical claim can be true.

steps.title: Ink covers the hole, so it is not a hole
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers רב אחא: he did not know the rule from ארץ ישראל that a hole the ink passes over does not count as a hole.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא missed what they say in ארץ ישראל: any hole that the ink passes over is not considered a hole.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רב אחא's question from the last step. Tiny hair holes do not ruin the letters of תפילין, because the ink covers them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אחא assumed that any hole in the parchment ruins the letter written over it. The rule from ארץ ישראל says a hole small enough for ink to flow over is not a hole at all. So רבי יוחנן's claim that hair goes through the hide survives.

keyTerms.meaning: It slipped past him; he did not know or remember it
'The West,' meaning ארץ ישראל
A hole or perforation
Ink

phrases.english: That which they say in the West escaped him:
phrases.notes: 'Him' is רב אחא, and 'the West' means ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: Any hole that the ink passes over
is not a hole.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אחא's objection in step 6
steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings a known rule that removes the problem
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב אחא thought hair holes would make תפילין parchment unusable
steps.terutzMaskana: A hole that ink covers is not a hole, so hair holes are no problem

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's proof from a hair across from meat
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן challenges ריש לקיש from a משנה: touching a hair across from an olive-size of meat on a hide makes a person טמא. Isn't that because hair is a שומר?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן challenged ריש לקיש: A hide with an olive-size of meat on it: one who touches a strand coming out of the meat, or a hair across from the meat, is טמא. Isn't this because the hair is a שומר?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן now goes on the attack. He quotes a משנה that seems to prove that hair is a שומר, which goes against ריש לקיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Touching only a hair, without touching the meat itself, still makes the person טמא. The easiest explanation is that the hair counts as a שומר and is treated as part of the meat. That is exactly what ריש לקיש denied in step 2.

keyTerms.meaning: An olive-size, the minimum amount of meat that can make a person impure
A thin strand or fiber of meat
Ritually impure
A protective covering, which counts together with the food it protects
'Is it not...?' The גמרא is suggesting the obvious reading

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan challenged Reish Lakish:
A hide that has an olive-size of meat on it,
one who touches a strand coming out of it,
or a hair opposite it, is impure.
phrases.notes: The hair is on the other side of the hide, right across from the meat.

phrases.english: Is it not because it is a protection?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending his own view, רבי יוחנן now attacks ריש לקיש's view
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's claim (step 2) that hair is not a שומר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Touching only a hair across from the meat makes one טמא, which suggests the hair is a שומר joined to the meat

steps.title: The hair is a handle, not a protection
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא deflects: the hair makes one טמא because it is a יד (handle) for the meat, not because it is a שומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is because the hair is a handle.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends ריש לקיש. The hair counts because it works as a handle for the meat, not as a protection.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A יד is a separate category: something you can hold to lift the food also passes on impurity. So the משנה can be explained without saying hair is a שומר. ריש לקיש's view stands.

keyTerms.meaning: A handle; something attached to food that you can hold it by, which passes on impurity
No; the גמרא rejects the suggested reading
Because of

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up יד and שומר. Both pass impurity to the food, but for different reasons: a שומר protects the food, while a יד is something you hold it by. The question here is only which one the hair is.

phrases.english: No, because it is a handle.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יוחנן's challenge on behalf of ריש לקיש
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets the reason behind the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The hair makes one טמא because it is a שומר
steps.terutzMaskana: The hair makes one טמא because it is a יד, so there is no proof against ריש לקיש

steps.title: How can one hair be a handle?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: what use is a single hair as a handle? You cannot lift meat with one hair.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is one hair good for?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the answer it just gave. A single hair seems too weak to hold anything, so how can it be a handle?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A יד only counts if it can actually be used to hold or lift the food. One thin hair would just pull out. This question sets up the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A single hair
One
What is it good for? What use does it have?

phrases.english: One hair, what is it good for?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions how the 'handle' answer of step 9 works
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How a single hair can function as a handle

steps.title: A hair among many hairs
steps.stepSummary: The answer borrows רבי אילעא's idea: just as he explained 'an awn' to mean an awn among many awns, here the משנה means a hair among many hairs.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי אילעא said, the case is an awn among the awns. Here too, the case is a hair among the hairs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה is talking about one hair that sits among many hairs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When there are many hairs, you can hold a bunch of them and lift the meat, so the hairs together act as a handle. The one hair a person touches is part of that handle, so it passes on impurity. The idea is copied from רבי אילעא's explanation of a similar case.

keyTerms.meaning: An awn: the thin bristle sticking out of a head of grain
That is among / between
So too; the same applies here

phrases.english: As Rabbi Ila said:
It is about an awn among the awns,
so too, it is about a hair among the hairs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה is talking about a hair among many hairs, which together can serve as a handle
steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש survives רבי יוחנן's challenge: the hair across from the meat counts as a יד (handle), because it sits among many hairs, and not as a שומר.

steps.title: Where רבי אילעא originally said this
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows the source of רבי אילעא's statement: a משנה about awns on grain stalks, which pass on and receive impurity but do not combine with the grain.
steps.simpleTranslation: And where was רבי אילעא's statement said? On this משנה: The awns on the stalks pass on impurity and become impure, but do not join together. What is an awn good for? רבי אילעא said: it is about an awn among the awns.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to show where רבי אילעא's idea first came from, so we understand the case it was borrowed from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The awns on a grain stalk are treated as a יד for the grain: they pass on impurity, but they are not counted as food to make up the minimum size. The same question came up there: how can one awn be a handle? רבי אילעא answered that it is an awn among many awns, just like the hair case.

keyTerms.meaning: Where
Stalks or heads of grain
They pass impurity on to others and can become impure themselves
Join together, combining to reach a minimum amount

phrases.english: And where was Rabbi Ila's statement said?
On this, which we learned in a Mishnah:
The awns that are on the stalks
pass on impurity and become impure
but do not join together.
phrases.notes: They don't count toward the minimum amount of food needed for impurity; only the grain itself counts.

phrases.english: An awn, what is it good for?
Rabbi Ila said:
It is about an awn among the awns.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the original source of the רבי אילעא statement used in step 11
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Where רבי אילעא's statement was originally said
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: On the משנה about awns on grain stalks, where he explained that the case is an awn among many awns

steps.title: What is the רוטב in the משנה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next word of the משנה, רוטב, and asks what it means.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'and the רוטב.' What is רוטב?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new item in the משנה's list and asks what the word רוטב means. This sets up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists things that join with meat to make the size of an egg for טומאת אוכלין, even though they do not count as food alone. To know which substance fits that rule, we first need to define רוטב.

keyTerms.meaning: Usually 'gravy'; here the גמרא will ask which kind of fat or liquid from meat it means

phrases.english: And the gravy.
What is 'gravy'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic. The discussion of hair and awns is done, and the גמרא moves to the next item in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the word רוטב in the משנה.

steps.title: רבא: it is the fat
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that רוטב means the fat.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: It is the fat.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question: רוטב is the fat that floats on top of the meat soup.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבא, this fat is a side product of the meat that joins with it to reach the size of an egg. The next step will challenge whether such fat can really belong on this list.

keyTerms.meaning: Fat (the fat floating on a meat broth)

phrases.english: Rava said: The fat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13.

steps.title: אביי: that fat is food by itself
steps.stepSummary: אביי objects that floating fat is food, so it would become טמא by itself and would not need to 'join' with anything.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: That fat itself should become טמא with טומאת אוכלין!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רבא's definition. Floating fat is eaten, so it counts as food on its own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists רוטב among things that only join with meat but are not food alone. If רוטב were edible fat, it would be full food and become טמא by itself. So it does not fit the משנה's list.

keyTerms.meaning: Food impurity, which applies to anything that counts as food, at the size of an egg
It itself, meaning on its own without joining with anything

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
It itself should be susceptible to impurity of food!
phrases.notes: He means: fat is something people eat, so why would the משנה need it to 'join' with the meat?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's answer in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's definition of רוטב as floating fat.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Edible fat is full food and would be טמא on its own. But the משנה lists רוטב as something that only joins with meat, so רבא's definition contradicts the משנה.

steps.title: אביי's definition: congealed fat
steps.stepSummary: אביי offers his own definition: רוטב is fat that oozed out of the meat and congealed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means fat that congealed.
steps.whatsHappening: Having rejected רבא's answer, אביי gives a new definition of רוטב: fat that congealed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Congealed fat that oozed out of the meat is not something people eat, so it is not food on its own. It can still join with the meat to reach the size of an egg. That fits the משנה exactly.

keyTerms.meaning: Fat that has congealed and hardened (not normally eaten)

phrases.english: Rather, it is fat that congealed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רבא's rejected definition with a new one that fits the משנה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רוטב is congealed fat, which is not food alone but joins with the meat.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't read חלב here as the forbidden fat of an animal. It simply means fat from the meat that hardened.

steps.title: Why only congealed? Liquid should combine too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the fat must be congealed. ריש לקיש taught that brine on a vegetable combines with it for the size needed on יום הכפורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why specifically congealed? Even when it is not congealed it should also combine! For ריש לקיש said: Brine on a vegetable combines to make the size of a large date on יום הכפורים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges אביי's detail that the fat must be congealed. It brings ריש לקיש's rule that a liquid on food combines with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's answer suggests liquid fat would not join the meat. But ריש לקיש says a liquid, the brine, joins the vegetable for the כותבת measure on יום הכפורים. If so, liquid fat should also join the meat, and the משנה would not need congealed fat.

keyTerms.meaning: Why specifically? Why mention this detail?
Brine, the salty liquid on pickled or cooked food
Combines, joins together to reach a required size
The size of a large date, the measure for liability for eating on יום הכפורים

phrases.english: Why specifically congealed?
Even when it is not congealed, too!
As Reish Lakish said:
Brine that is on a vegetable
combines to make a large date-bulk on Yom Kippur.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי אִירְיָא קְרִישׁ? כִּי לָא קְרִישׁ נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the specific detail 'congealed' in אביי's definition from step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The requirement that the fat be congealed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ריש לקיש shows that a liquid on food combines with that food. So liquid fat should combine with meat too, and the word 'congealed' would be unnecessary.

steps.title: יום הכפורים is about settling the mind
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that יום הכפורים is different. There the measure depends on whether a person's mind is settled, and anything at all settles it.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it is because of settling the mind. With anything at all, his mind is settled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof from ריש לקיש. It explains that the rule of יום הכפורים works for its own special reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On יום הכפורים, the measure for eating is set by whether the eating settles a person's mind, so even brine adds to that feeling. Food impurity has no such reason, so ריש לקיש's rule does not carry over. That is why the משנה needs congealed fat to join the meat.

keyTerms.meaning: Settling the mind, the feeling of satisfaction from eating
With anything at all, however little

phrases.english: There, it is because of settling the mind,
phrases.notes: 'There' means the יום הכפורים case of ריש לקיש.

phrases.english: and with anything at all his mind is settled.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 17 by limiting ריש לקיש's rule to יום הכפורים.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (חילוק): the rule for יום הכפורים has its own reason.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since a liquid combines with food on יום הכפורים, liquid fat should combine with meat for טומאת אוכלין too.
steps.terutzMaskana: On יום הכפורים anything that settles the mind counts, even a liquid. For טומאת אוכלין that reason does not apply, so only congealed fat joins the meat.

steps.title: For impurity the fat has to be congealed to join

steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the answer it began in step 18. It explains why the brine rule of יום הכפורים does not apply to impurity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On יום הכפורים, anything that settles the mind counts, so even liquid brine adds to the size. For טומאה, the fat has to truly join with the meat to make up the size of an egg, and a liquid cannot join with solid food. So the fat must be congealed, which supports אביי's definition from step 16.

steps.title: Why the Torah needed 'soul' in all three places
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins explaining why each of the three uses of נפש is needed. חמץ and נבלה could not be learned from חלב alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: And all three are needed. If the Torah had written it only about חלב, we could not learn חמץ from it, since חלב never had a time when it was permitted. And we could not learn נבלה from it, since חלב is punished with כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers an unasked question: why did the Torah need to write נפש three times? It starts by showing that חלב alone would not teach us the other two.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חלב is stricter than חמץ, because חלב was never allowed to be eaten, while חמץ is allowed before פסח. חלב is also stricter than נבלה, because eating חלב brings כרת and eating נבלה does not. A stricter case cannot teach a lighter one, so each case needs its own word.

steps.terutzMaskana: חלב has strictnesses that חמץ and נבלה lack, so they cannot be learned from it

steps.title: חמץ alone could not teach חלב or נבלה
steps.stepSummary: If the Torah had written נפש only by חמץ, we could not learn חלב from it, because חמץ is never permitted in any case. We also could not learn נבלה from it, because חמץ carries כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the Torah had written it only by חמץ, we couldn't learn חלב from it, since חמץ never has a permitted version. We couldn't learn נבלה from it either, since חמץ is punished with כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues showing why each of the three mentions of נפש is needed. Here it tests what would happen if only חמץ had been written.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חמץ has two strict features: it has no permitted form, while חלב of a wild animal is allowed. It is also punished with כרת, which נבלה is not. Because of these, a law said about חמץ could just be a special strictness of חמץ, so it can't be carried over to the others.

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One, meaning the Torah
Leavened bread, forbidden on פסח
Forbidden fat of certain animals
Never permitted out of its general prohibition; it has no allowed version
Spiritual cutting off, a severe punishment from Heaven

phrases.english: And if the Merciful One had written [it only by] chametz
phrases.notes: "It" means the extra word נפש, which teaches that drinking counts.

phrases.english: forbidden fat could not be learned from it,
since it was never permitted out of its general rule,
phrases.notes: חלב does have a permitted version, the fat of a wild animal. חמץ has none.

phrases.english: and a carcass could not be learned from it,
since it is punished with karet.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the explanation from step 35 of why each mention of נפש is needed, now testing חמץ as the only source.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing a special strictness that blocks a comparison
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe writing נפש by חמץ alone would be enough to teach חלב and נבלה.
steps.terutzMaskana: חמץ is stricter (no permitted form, and כרת), so it cannot teach the others.

steps.title: A carcass alone could not teach the other two
steps.stepSummary: If the Torah had written נפש only by נבלה, we could not learn חלב and חמץ from it, because נבלה makes a person טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the Torah had written it only by נבלה, we couldn't learn the other two from it, since נבלה makes a person טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the list by testing נבלה as the only source. This completes the proof that each of the three mentions is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נבלה has a strictness the other two lack: eating it makes a person טמא. So a rule written about נבלה might come only from that strictness. Each case is now shown to have its own unique strict point.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal carcass that died without proper שחיטה
It makes a person or thing ritually impure
Those, meaning the other two cases

steps.whatToRemember: Each of the three has its own strictness: חלב never had a time when it was permitted and carries כרת; חמץ has no permitted form and carries כרת; and נבלה makes one טמא. So none can be learned from just one other.

phrases.english: And if the Merciful One had written [it only] by a carcass
those could not be learned from it,
phrases.notes: "Those" are חלב and חמץ.

phrases.english: since it makes a person impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the three-way check started in step 35 and continued in step 36.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing a special strictness that blocks a comparison
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe writing נפש by נבלה alone would be enough.
steps.terutzMaskana: נבלה makes one טמא, so it cannot teach חלב or חמץ.

steps.title: Why not learn one case from the other two together?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: fine, one case can't teach one other case. But two cases together should be able to teach the third.
steps.simpleTranslation: One can't be learned from one. But let one be learned from two!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the idea that all three mentions are needed. It suggests the Torah could have written two and let us learn the third from them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When two cases are put together, the special strictness of each one is canceled out by the other. So the challenge is that one of the three mentions of נפש seems extra. This sets up a check of each possible option.

keyTerms.meaning: One from one, learning one case from a single other case
Let it come, meaning let it be learned
From two, learning from two cases together

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new question about drinking. It only asks whether all three Torah mentions are really needed, or whether one is extra.

phrases.english: One cannot be learned from one,
let one be learned from two!

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲדָא מֵחֲדָא לָא אָתְיָא, תֵּיתֵי חֲדָא מִתַּרְתֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion of steps 36-37 that all three mentions are needed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that each of the three mentions of נפש is necessary.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two cases together cancel out each other's unique strictness, so the third should be learnable from them, making one mention extra.

steps.title: A carcass cannot be learned from fat and chametz
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers by asking which one we would learn. Not נבלה, because חלב and חמץ both carry כרת, and נבלה does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which one would you learn? Should the Torah not write it by נבלה and learn it from the other two? No, because those two are punished with כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins answering the challenge by checking each option one by one. First it tries leaving out נבלה, and rejects it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Learning from two only works if they don't share a strictness that the third case lacks. חלב and חמץ both carry כרת, but נבלה doesn't. So a rule about the two could come from their כרת, and it can't be carried over to נבלה.

keyTerms.meaning: Which one would you learn?
Let it not write, meaning the Torah could have left it out
What about these? The opening of a refutation
A refutation that shows why a comparison fails

phrases.english: Which one would you learn?
Let the Merciful One not write [it] by a carcass
and learn it from these?
phrases.notes: "These" are חלב and חמץ.

phrases.english: What about these? They are punished with karet!

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵי תֵּיתֵי? לָא לִכְתּוֹב רַחֲמָנָא בִּנְבֵלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to step 38 by testing the first option, נבלה, and showing it fails.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Checking each option and finding a shared strictness that blocks it
steps.terutzHavaAmina: נבלה could be learned from חלב and חמץ together.
steps.terutzMaskana: חלב and חמץ share כרת, which נבלה lacks, so נבלה must be written on its own.

steps.title: Chametz cannot be learned from fat and a carcass
steps.stepSummary: Next the גמרא tries leaving out חמץ and learning it from חלב and נבלה. This fails too, because those two never had a time when they were fit to eat, while חמץ did.
steps.simpleTranslation: Should the Torah not write it by חמץ and learn it from the other two? No, because those two never had a time when they were fit to eat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues checking the options. Now it tries leaving out חמץ, and rejects that too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חלב and נבלה share a feature: they were never allowed to be eaten at any point. חמץ was fine to eat before פסח, which makes it more lenient in this way. So a rule found by the two strict ones can't be carried over to חמץ. Two of the three options have now been ruled out.

keyTerms.meaning: A time of fitness, a period when the food was allowed to be eaten
Fitness, being proper to use or eat
To them, meaning fat and the carcass

phrases.english: Let the Merciful One not write [it] by chametz,
and learn it from these?
phrases.notes: Now "these" are חלב and נבלה.

phrases.english: What about these?

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁכֵּן לֹא הָיְתָה לָהֶן שְׁעַת הַכּוֹשֶׁר!
phrases.english: They never had a time when they were fit to eat!
phrases.notes: חמץ was fine to eat before פסח. חלב and נבלה were never allowed.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא לִכְתּוֹב רַחֲמָנָא בְּחָמֵץ, וְתֵיתֵי מֵהָנָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the option-by-option answer from step 39, now testing חמץ.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Checking each option and finding a shared strictness that blocks it
steps.terutzHavaAmina: חמץ could be learned from חלב and נבלה together.
steps.terutzMaskana: חלב and נבלה never had a time when they were fit to eat, unlike חמץ, so חמץ must be written on its own.

steps.title: Leaving out חלב also fails
steps.stepSummary: We cannot learn חלב from חמץ and נבלה, because those were never permitted in any situation, while חלב was.
steps.simpleTranslation: Maybe the Torah should not write it by חלב, and we would learn it from these two? No. These two were never permitted in any way. Can you say the same about חלב, which was permitted in some way?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the last option: leave out חלב and learn it from חמץ and נבלה. It rejects this too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חמץ and נבלה share a strict feature: their general ban was never lifted in any situation. חלב is weaker, because part of its ban was lifted. So a weaker case cannot be learned from stricter ones, and all three mentions of נפש are needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Let the Torah not write it here (and learn it from somewhere else instead)
And learn it from these other cases
What about these? (they have a special feature that the new case lacks)
Part of its general ban was lifted in some situation

phrases.english: Let the Merciful One not write it by חלב,
and learn it from these (חמץ and נבלה).

phrases.aramaic: מָה לְהָנָךְ שֶׁכֵּן לֹא הוּתַּר מִכְּלָלָן,
phrases.english: What about these? Their general ban was never lifted in any situation.
Can you say the same about חלב, whose general ban was lifted in some situation?

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא לִכְתּוֹב רַחֲמָנָא בְּחֵלֶב, וְתֵיתֵי מֵהָנָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third and final attempt to learn one case from the other two, following steps 39 and 40.
steps.terutzResolutionType: פירכא: the source cases are stricter than the case being learned
steps.terutzHavaAmina: חלב could be learned from חמץ and נבלה.
steps.terutzMaskana: חלב was partly permitted, so it cannot be learned from them. נפש must be written by all three.

steps.title: In what way was חלב permitted?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which situation is meant when it says חלב was permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is that situation?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what it meant by saying חלב was permitted. This question sets up the next few steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 41 depends on חלב having a permitted case that נבלה lacks. Now the גמרא must name that case. It must also make sure נבלה has nothing similar, or the answer would fall apart.

keyTerms.meaning: And what is it? (a request to identify exactly what is meant)

phrases.english: And what is it?
phrases.notes: He means: which situation do we mean when we say חלב was permitted?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the claim made in step 41.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which situation lifts part of the ban on חלב?

steps.title: Not fat offered on the מזבח
steps.stepSummary: If the permitted case is fat offered to ה׳‎, נבלה has the same thing, because a bird killed by מליקה is offered on the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is the fat of a domestic animal, which is allowed on the מזבח, then נבלה is also allowed there: a bird killed by מליקה is offered on the מזבח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests the permitted case is the fat of a בהמה offered on the מזבח. It rejects this, because נבלה also has a case like that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מליקה is not שחיטה, so a bird killed this way would normally be נבלה. Yet it is the proper way to bring a bird קרבן. So נבלה is also 'permitted for גבוה,' and חלב is no different.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (a suggestion that is about to be rejected)
For the Most High, meaning offered on the מזבח
Killing a bird קרבן by pinching the back of its neck, not by שחיטה

phrases.english: If you say it is the fat of a domestic animal, permitted for the Most High,
then נבלה was also permitted:
a bird killed by מליקה is offered to the Most High.
phrases.notes: A bird without שחיטה counts as נבלה, yet this is how bird קרבנות are brought.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First proposed answer to the question in step 42, rejected.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects 'permitted for the מזבח' as the difference between חלב and נבלה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: נבלה is also permitted for the מזבח through מליקה.

steps.title: Wild-animal fat seems to fail too
steps.stepSummary: If the permitted case is the fat of a wild animal, נבלה seems to match it, because כהנים eat a חטאת העוף killed by מליקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is the fat of a wild animal, which an ordinary person may eat. But נבלה was also permitted to people: a חטאת העוף killed by מליקה is eaten by the כהנים!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests the fat of a חיה, which anyone may eat. It challenges this too, since a kind of נבלה is eaten by people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חלב of a חיה is permitted for regular eating. But the bird חטאת is killed by מליקה, so it looks like נבלה, and the כהנים eat its meat. So נבלה would also be 'permitted to people,' and the difference disappears.

keyTerms.meaning: Fat of a wild animal, which is permitted to eat
An ordinary person, as opposed to the מזבח
A bird brought as a חטאת; the כהנים eat its meat

phrases.english: Rather, it is the fat of a wild animal, permitted to an ordinary person.
But נבלה was also permitted:
the מליקה of a bird חטאת makes it permitted for the כהנים!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second proposed answer to step 42, also challenged.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Challenges 'permitted to people' as the difference.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: כהנים eat the bird חטאת even though it was killed by מליקה.

steps.title: כהנים eat from ה׳'s table
steps.stepSummary: The answer is the fat of a wild animal. The כהנים are not a problem, because they receive their share from the מזבח's portion.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, it is the fat of a wild animal, permitted to an ordinary person. And what bothered you about the כהנים: the כהנים receive their share from the table of the Most High.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps the second answer, wild-animal fat. It explains why the כהנים eating the bird חטאת does not count as נבלה being permitted to people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כהנים do not eat as ordinary people. They take a share of what was given to ה׳. So the bird is permitted to them only as part of the מזבח's permission, which is the case we already discussed. נבלה is never permitted to a regular person, but חלב חיה is. That difference holds.

keyTerms.meaning: Really; actually (we go back to the earlier suggestion)
And what was difficult for you
They receive their share from the table of the Most High

steps.whatToRemember: חלב is different from חמץ and נבלה because the fat of a wild animal is permitted to ordinary people. כהנים eating the מליקה bird does not count, because they eat from 'ה׳'s table.' So נפש had to be written by all three.

phrases.english: Really, it is the fat of a wild animal, permitted to an ordinary person,
and what was difficult for you about the כהנים:
the כהנים receive their share from the table of the Most High.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 44 and keeps its suggestion.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the כהנים eat as part of the מזבח's share
steps.terutzHavaAmina: כהנים eating the מליקה bird means נבלה is permitted to people.
steps.terutzMaskana: כהנים eat from ה׳'s table, so only חלב (of a חיה) is truly permitted to ordinary people.

steps.title: Why does the ברייתא need a word to forbid the liquids of שרצים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that learns from the word ״הַטְּמֵאִים״ that the juice, gravy and sediment of שרצים are forbidden. It asks why a word is needed, since we could learn this from the cases of melted חלב, נבלה and חמץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא says: the word ״הַטְּמֵאִים״ teaches that the juice, the gravy and the sediment of שרצים are forbidden. Why do we need this word? Let us learn it from these other cases.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges a ברייתא. If liquid forms of forbidden foods are already forbidden, why does the תורה need an extra word for the liquids of שרצים?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The steps before this one showed that melted חלב, liquid נבלה and dissolved חמץ still count as forbidden food. If so, the same idea should cover the liquids of שרצים without a special word. The ברייתא's use of ״הַטְּמֵאִים״ therefore looks unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: Small creeping creatures that the תורה forbids eating
Their juice, the liquid that oozes out of them
Their gravy, the liquid that forms when they are cooked
Sediment, the thick part that settles at the bottom of a cooked dish
Why do I need it? This asks why a source or word is needed at all
Let it be learned (from another case)

phrases.english: But that which is taught in a ברייתא:
"That are impure" comes to forbid their juice
phrases.notes: ויקרא 11:31, about שרצים. The ברייתא learns this from the extra letter ה at the start of the word.

phrases.english: and their gravy and their sediment.
Why do I need this? Let it be learned from these!
phrases.notes: "These" are the earlier cases of melted חלב, liquid נבלה and dissolved חמץ.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the discussion of חלב, נבלה and חמץ to a ברייתא about שרצים that seems to repeat what those cases already teach.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא that uses ״הַטְּמֵאִים״ to forbid the liquids of שרצים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the liquid forms of other forbidden foods are already forbidden, the liquids of שרצים could be learned from them. That would make the extra word unnecessary.

steps.title: The word is needed so the liquids are not limited to a כזית
steps.stepSummary: The word is necessary. Without it, we would learn the law from the other cases, and the דַּיּוֹ rule would say the punishment applies only at a כזית, as in those cases. The word teaches that the regular שרץ amount applies.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is necessary. If the תורה had not written it, I would have said: it is enough for a law learned from another case to be like that case. Just as there, a person is not punished until there is a כזית, so too here, a person is not punished until there is a כזית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the word ״הַטְּמֵאִים״ is needed. Learning from the other cases would only give the larger amount needed there, a כזית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A law learned from another case can be no stricter than that case. This is the rule of דַּיּוֹ לַבָּא מִן הַדִּין לִהְיוֹת כַּנִּדּוֹן. Since חלב, נבלה and חמץ need a כזית, the liquids of שרצים would also need a כזית. The separate word shows they follow the usual smaller שרץ amount, a lentil-size (כעדשה).

keyTerms.meaning: It is necessary. The extra source is needed after all
The Merciful One, a name for ה׳ as the Giver of the תורה
I would have thought. This is the mistaken idea we would have had without the source

keyTerms.term: דַּיּוֹ לַבָּא מִן הַדִּין לִהְיוֹת כַּנִּדּוֹן
keyTerms.meaning: It is enough for what is learned from a case to be like that case. A learned law cannot be stricter than its source
An olive-size, the usual amount for being punished for eating forbidden food

steps.whatToRemember: The word ״הַטְּמֵאִים״ is not extra. Without it, the דַּיּוֹ rule would require a כזית for the liquids of שרצים. With it, they follow the normal שרץ amount.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the question is whether the liquids are forbidden at all. Both sides agree they are forbidden. The answer is only about how much a person must eat to be punished.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common pattern in the גמרא: a source that looks extra can be needed to avoid the limits of the דַּיּוֹ rule.

phrases.english: It is necessary,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִי לָא כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא – הֲוָה אָמֵינָא:
phrases.english: for if the Merciful One had not written it, I would have said:

phrases.aramaic: דַּיּוֹ לַבָּא מִן הַדִּין לִהְיוֹת כַּנִּדּוֹן,
phrases.english: it is enough for what comes from the inference to be like the case it was learned from.
Just as there, one is not punished until there is an olive-size,
phrases.notes: "There" means the melted חלב, נבלה and חמץ.

phrases.aramaic: אַף הָכָא נָמֵי – עַד דְּאִיכָּא כְּזַיִת.
phrases.english: so too here, one is not punished until there is an olive-size.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 46 by showing that the word ״הַטְּמֵאִים״ teaches something the other cases cannot.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the source is needed (צריכותא) because of the limit of the דַּיּוֹ rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Learning from חלב, נבלה and חמץ, the liquids of שרצים would require a כזית before a person is punished.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word ״הַטְּמֵאִים״ teaches that the liquids of שרצים follow the normal smaller שרץ amount, not a כזית.
